title: Texture replacement expands PCSX2 visual modding
summary: PCSX2 added a managed texture dump and replacement workflow that lets community packs refresh artwork without rewriting a game's executable.
heroAlt: Texture replacement expands PCSX2 visual modding
searchKeywords: Texture replacement expands PCSX2 visual modding

blocks.text: Why resolution scaling is not enough

Raising PCSX2's internal resolution sharpens geometry and framebuffer effects, but it cannot restore detail that is absent from a game's original texture. Texture replacement intercepts identified source textures and supplies authored high-resolution assets before the renderer samples them.

PCSX2 can dump texture data with identifiers used by the replacement loader. Pack authors edit those exports and preserve the expected naming so the emulator can match them during later runs. The original game image remains unchanged; the pack is an optional local layer.

Some PS2 games generate or rewrite textures in ways that produce changing hashes. The project warns that those assets may not be replaceable and that more accurate GS emulation can change identifiers. Pack maintainers must be prepared to update data rather than expecting one hash scheme forever.

High-resolution packs can consume substantially more VRAM and may introduce seams or incorrect artwork independent of PCSX2. The official community does not treat pack bugs as emulator bugs and asks users to take rendering issues to the pack author after reproducing them without replacements.

The feature changes artwork, not game geometry, executable logic or compatibility fixes. That boundary explains both its power and its limits: a carefully authored pack can refresh text and surfaces, but it cannot repair a broken effect that depends on blend equations or framebuffer behavior. A dependable pack therefore records the game revision, source hashes and PCSX2 behavior it was tested against. Before blaming the renderer, users can disable replacements and compare the same scene at the same internal resolution. That controlled check separates an incorrectly named or edited asset from a genuine graphics regression and gives both pack authors and emulator developers evidence they can reproduce.
